description: New Zealand average domestic university tuition fees per Equivalent Full-Time Student (EFTS), in NZD, annual. Data from Ministry of Education (Education Counts) and TEC. Government imposed a fee freeze 2000-2003, then Fee and Course Costs Maxima (FCCM) from 2004. Fees First Year Free policy introduced 2018 (first year of tertiary study free for eligible students).
source: New Zealand Ministry of Education (Education Counts), Tertiary Education Commission (TEC)
note: Average domestic tuition fee per EFTS across all public universities. Individual institution fees vary. Fees First Year Free (FFF) policy from 2018 means many domestic students pay $0 in their first year; average fee data for 2018+ reflects sticker prices not net costs. Maximum Student Contribution (MSC) rates set by TEC define the ceiling per EFTS per subject band.

maximumStudentContribution.note: TEC Maximum Student Contribution rates (MSC) per EFTS for universities, by subject band. These are the legal maximum that providers can charge. Most universities charge at or near the maximum.

policyTimeline.event: Tuition fees introduced following 1990 tertiary education reforms; fees rose rapidly through 1990s
Government-imposed fee freeze: no increases allowed 2000-2003
Fee and Course Costs Maxima (FCCM) introduced: government cap on annual fee increases based on inflation
Annual Maximum Fee Movement (AMFM) policy refined
Fees First Year Free (FFF): first year of post-school education free for eligible students. ~60,000 students benefit annually.
Ongoing FFF policy, fees increasing within AMFM cap (~3-4% per year)

keyFacts: Fees introduced 1991; more than tripled through the 1990s before freeze
FCCM cap since 2004 limits annual increases to ~3-4% per year
Fees First Year Free (2018-present) means ~60,000 students pay zero tuition in first year
Average university fee ~NZD 7,050 per EFTS in 2024 (sticker price)
Net cost substantially lower for many students due to FFF and student allowances
